facts.text: The environment is registered as airsim-env-v0 with entry point gym_env.envs:AirsimGymEnv
AirsimGymEnv subclasses gym.Env and QtCore.QThread
The selected configuration sets env_name NH_center and dynamic_name SimpleMultirotor
The NH_center configuration sets navigation_3d True, using_velocity_state False, perception vector, dt 0.1 s, v_xy_min 0.5, v_xy_max 5, v_z_max 2.0 and yaw_rate_max_deg 30.0
The environment builds MultirotorDynamicsSimple when dynamic_name is SimpleMultirotor
With navigation_3d True and using_velocity_state False the multirotor state feature has 3 entries
The 3D action space is Box(low=[v_xy_min, -v_z_max, -yaw_rate_max_rad], high=[v_xy_max, v_z_max, yaw_rate_max_rad])
For NH_center the start position is [0, 0, 5], the goal rectangle is [-128, -128, 128, 128], the workspace is x [-140, 140], y [-140, 140], z [0.5, 20] and max_episode_steps is 1000
The configuration sets cnn_feature_num 25, crash_distance 1 and accept_radius 2
The declared vector observation space is Box(low=0, high=1, shape=(1, cnn_feature_num + state_feature_length))
The vector observation concatenates five depth-column maxima normalized to 0..1 with the normalized state feature and reshapes it to one row
An action step updates x, y, z and yaw by dt and wraps yaw beyond plus or minus pi
The start yaw is start_random_angle times a uniform random number
AirsimGymEnv.reset returns only the observation
AirsimGymEnv.step returns (observation, reward, done, info)
is_done ends the episode on a workspace exit, a goal within accept_radius, a crash, or step_num at max_episode_steps
compute_reward_final uses distance_reward_coef 500 for NH_center, reward_reach 10, reward_crash -20 and reward_outside -10
compute_reward_final subtracts 0.1 times punishment_pose, 0.2 times punishment_obs, 0.1 times punishment_action and 0.5 times yaw_error_cost
A collision is reported when AirSim reports has_collided or the minimum obstacle distance is below crash_distance
The README states Python 3.8, AirSim 1.6.0, PyTorch 1.10.1, gym 0.21.0 and PyQt5 5.15.6

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the start yaw and the goal draw, and the kinematic update is deterministic, so the fake repeats a trajectory for one seed and action list; the upstream draws those two values from numpy's global generator, so a seed gives different trajectories on the two implementations

gaps: no AirSim scene, physics engine, depth image, collision query or rendering: the fake advances the kinematic MultirotorDynamicsSimple state in pure Python and returns five placeholder depth features (marked in fake.py); the upstream observation derives those five features from a depth image

the upstream declares observation_space shape (1, cnn_feature_num + state_feature_length) = (1, 28) for this configuration (airsim_env.py:180-185, config line 18), but get_obs_vector returns five depth features plus the three state features (airsim_env.py:394-425); the fake publishes the actual 8-value vector
the fake draws the start yaw and the goal with Python's random.Random; upstream uses numpy's global generator, so one seed gives different trajectories
no collision information: is_crashed uses only the placeholder minimum distance, not AirSim's simGetCollisionInfo (airsim_env.py:896-902)
no PyQt signals and no AirSim RPC; the fake was not compared with the upstream environment, which needs AirSim 1.6.0, gym 0.21.0, PyQt5 and torch (README.md:58-66)
the sim backend was not run: it needs the upstream package and an AirSim scene, and the upstream environment needs set_config(cfg) before it has spaces, which the family bridge does not call

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: while the e-stop is latched, step and reset calls are refused with MHS.SAFETY.ESTOP_ENGAGED and the last state stays readable; only mhs.safety.reset clears the latch
